antiphen_syrup.notes: Quick calc: BW÷4 ~ BW÷2 mL/dose; space doses ≥4 hours apart; may stagger with Ibuprofen by half an hour

clinical.warnings: Max 75 mg/kg/day; space doses ≥4 hr apart; do not combine with other acetaminophen-containing products

acetaminophen_tab.notes: Max 1#/dose; tablets are usually only started at ≥30 kg

clinical.warnings: Tablets usually only started at ≥30 kg; max 4 g/day (children 75 mg/kg/day)

idefen_syrup.notes: Quick calc: BW÷4 ~ BW÷2 mL/dose; contraindicated < 6 months; for use ≥ 6 months-12 years

clinical.contraindications: <6 months, GI ulcer, aspirin triad (asthma+rhinitis+nasal polyp), severe renal/hepatic failure
clinical.adverseEffects: GI upset, GI bleeding, acute kidney injury, decreased platelet function
clinical.warnings: Contraindicated <6 months; use with caution during dehydration/prerenal hypoperfusion; max 40 mg/kg/day

voren_supp.notes: Quick calc: BW÷25 ~ BW÷12.5 supp; Max 2 supp/day; backup antipyretic for infants/young children

contraindications.reason: NSAID — GI bleeding / nephrotoxicity; limit to backup antipyretic use in infants/young children

clinical.contraindications: Active GI bleeding, severe renal failure, aspirin triad
clinical.adverseEffects: GI upset, rectal irritation, rare abnormal liver function
clinical.warnings: Max 2 supp/day; when fever has not resolved, do not repeat PR + PO NSAID within a short interval

clinical.use: Nasal congestion/rhinorrhea from common cold (combination product)
clinical.contraindications: Current MAOI therapy, severe HTN, CAD, hyperthyroidism
clinical.adverseEffects: Drowsiness, dry mouth, stimulation (from the pseudoephedrine component)
clinical.warnings: <2y not recommended; monitor BP/HR due to pseudoephedrine content

cypromin_syrup.notes: First-generation antihistamine; may switch to cetirizine in older children

clinical.use: Allergy, rhinorrhea, itching; also used for poor appetite
clinical.adverseEffects: Drowsiness, dry mouth, weight gain (increased appetite)
clinical.warnings: First-generation antihistamine with pronounced sedative effect
clinical.breastfeeding: Short-term use acceptable (may reduce milk supply)

cetirizine_syrup.notes: Per label, by age band: <3y per physician's judgment (typically 0.25 mg/kg/dose); 3-6y 5 mg QD or 2.5 mg BID; ≥6y 10 mg QD. Halve the dose for renal impairment.

clinical.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to cetirizine / hydroxyzine; severe renal impairment (CrCl <10) requires adjustment
clinical.adverseEffects: Drowsiness (milder than first-generation), dry mouth, headache
clinical.warnings: Requires dose adjustment in renal impairment; assess before use under age 2
clinical.breastfeeding: Passes into breast milk; long-term use best avoided

cypromin_tab.notes: Converted from syrup 0.4 mg/mL × 0.6 mL/kg/day to 0.24 mg/kg/day; max 16 mg/day

clinical.warnings: First-generation antihistamine; watch for drowsiness

clinical.use: Symptomatic relief of common cold (combination product)
clinical.warnings: <2y not recommended; monitor BP/HR due to methylephedrine content

glyo_syrup.notes: Avoid <1 year (contains compound glycyrrhiza; contraindicated in young infants)

clinical.warnings: Avoid <1 year (contains compound glycyrrhiza); avoid prolonged high-dose use
Use with caution in asthma; separate from antibiotics by 1-2 hr

acc_effervescent.notes: 600mg mucolytic effervescent tablet; dissolve in water before drinking; <6 years recommend Actein granule 200mg/sachet instead

bands.dose: Not recommended (<6 years switch to Actein granule)

clinical.warnings: <6 years recommend switching to granule form; take immediately after dissolving in water

soltan_syrup.brand: Mucosolvan syrup (hospital mainly stocks Mubroxol tab)

clinical.warnings: Rare severe skin reactions (Stevens-Johnson syndrome)

zithromax_susp.notes: Quick calc: 0.25 mL/kg QD; reconstitute by adding 9mL water to make 15mL, shake well; stable at room temperature for 7 days after reconstitution
zithromax_susp.source: Lexicomp + KMUH quick-dose table + TCVGH PDF reference

clinical.adverseEffects: GI upset, taste disturbance, QT prolongation (high dose)
clinical.warnings: QT prolongation risk (consider baseline ECG); 3 days is sufficient for mycoplasma
QT prolongation risk; max 500 mg/day

amoxicillin_susp.notes: High dose for otitis media/CAP; simple URI may use 50 mg/kg/day; switch to capsule in older children

contraindications.reason: ≥ 30 kg switch to Amoxicillin 500 mg cap

clinical.adverseEffects: GI upset, rash (especially with EBV infection), rare anaphylaxis
clinical.warnings: High rash rate with EBV/IM infection; use high dose 80-90 mg/kg/day for otitis media/CAP
Capsules usually only started at ≥30 kg; high dose 80-90 mg/kg/day

curam_susp.notes: High dose for otitis media/CAP; 7:1 formulation reduces diarrhea; switch to tablet in older children
curam_susp.concentration_note: 60 mL/bottle, reconstitute with water before use; Amox 400 mg + Clav 57 mg / 5 mL (7:1 ratio)

clinical.contraindications: Penicillin hypersensitivity, history of cholestatic jaundice
clinical.adverseEffects: GI upset (especially diarrhea), rash, rare abnormal liver function
clinical.warnings: Clavulanate component prone to causing diarrhea; use 80-90 mg/kg/day (by amox) for otitis media/CAP

clinical.use: Otitis media, CAP, complicated URI (875/125 tab)
clinical.contraindications: Penicillin hypersensitivity, history of cholestatic jaundice
clinical.warnings: For use ≥30 kg; max 3 g/day amox

tamiflu.notes: Most effective when started within 48 hours of symptom onset; per Taiwan Pediatric Society antiviral guidance
tamiflu.concentration_note: Capsule strength varies by age/weight (30/45/75 mg)

contraindications.reason: < 2 weeks; insufficient safety data in neonates

clinical.use: Treatment and prophylaxis of influenza A/B
clinical.adverseEffects: N/V (most common), headache, rare neuropsychiatric events
clinical.warnings: Most effective within 48 hr of symptom onset; neuropsychiatric events are rare but caregivers should be counseled

rapiacta_iv.notes: ≥6 months: 10-12 mg/kg single dose; adult 600 mg. Option for influenza requiring hospitalization / unable to tolerate oral therapy; publicly funded version (2RAPIA) available during outbreak periods via the CDC, otherwise use the self-pay 2RAPI3 version
warnings: Dilute to 30-100 mL N/S, IV over 15-30 min

clinical.use: Treatment of influenza A/B (unable to tolerate oral therapy / severe disease)
clinical.warnings: For use ≥6 months; single IV infusion over 15-30 min; dose adjustment required for severe hepatic/renal impairment

xofluza_tab.notes: For use ≥1 year; single oral dose completes the course; do not take with dairy/calcium products (reduced absorption)
warnings: Most effective when taken within 48 hours of symptom onset

bands.dose: ≥1 year + <20 kg: 2 mg/kg PO single dose

clinical.use: Treatment of influenza A/B (single oral dose)
clinical.warnings: For use ≥1 year; do not co-administer with calcium/magnesium/iron-containing products (reduced absorption)

relenza_inh.notes: For use ≥7 years; administered via Diskhaler; use with caution in asthma/COPD (may trigger bronchospasm)
warnings: Use with caution in asthma/COPD — risk of triggering bronchospasm

contraindications.reason: < 7 years not recommended for the Diskhaler inhaled form

clinical.warnings: For use ≥7 years; may trigger bronchospasm in asthma patients — use a bronchodilator before administration
